sentences.text: Hesperosaurus is a herbivorous stegosaurian dinosaur whose name means "western lizard" in Ancient Greek.
This large stegosaur reached 6.5 meters in length and 3.5 metric tons in body mass, though Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight at 3.5 tons.
Its back plates were likely shorter than those of Stegosaurus but longer than average.
In 2001, Carpenter identified ten plates in the holotype, describing them as long and low.
The discovery of a plate sheath impression in Hesperosaurus represents the first direct proof of such structures in any stegosaurian.
Rows of small hexagonal, non-overlapping, convex scales measuring two to seven millimeters in diameter were found on the lower trunk flank.
Fossils of Hesperosaurus have been found in Wyoming and Montana, USA, since 1985.
Fossil hunter Patrick McSherry discovered the remains of a stegosaur in Johnson County, Wyoming, in 1985.
The species Hesperosaurus mjosi was named and described in 2001 by Kenneth Carpenter, Clifford Miles, and Karen Cloward.
In 2001, it represented the oldest known stegosaur in the United States.
The holotype skeleton shows healed fractures, indicating it belonged to an older individual, and the skeleton was partially articulated based on these healed fractures.

The holotype consists of an almost complete skull and much of the skeleton, including thirteen neck vertebrae, thirteen posterior vertebrae, three sacral vertebrae, forty-four tail vertebrae, dorsal ribs, chevrons, a complete pelvis, and ten plates from the neck and back.
The tail of Hesperosaurus ended with a thagomizer consisting of two pairs of spikes, with the front pair being thicker and the rear pair thinner and directed horizontally backward.
A 2012 histological study concluded that Hesperosaurus osteoderms are structurally identical to those of Stegosaurus.
Extensive long and wide arterial channels were observed in the bone structure of the plates.
Researchers suggest that the presence of a sheath on Hesperosaurus plates indicates a primary defensive function, as the horn layer would have strengthened the plate and provided sharp cutting edges.

A 2015 study by Evan Thomas Saitta concluded that Hesperosaurus exhibited sexual dimorphism based on finds from the JRDI 5ES Quarry, suggesting that tall back plates typified female Hesperosaurus while males were equipped with low broad plates.
Plates found at the quarry came in two types: one taller and one shorter.

A 2001 cladistic analysis by Carpenter showed that Hesperosaurus was rather basal and related to Dacentrurus, and Kenneth Carpenter originally concluded that Hesperosaurus was a fairly basal stegosaurid.
In 2010, Kenneth Carpenter rejected merging Hesperosaurus with Stegosaurus, arguing it was distinct enough to remain a separate genus.

Hesperosaurus lived approximately 152 million years ago during the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian stage in what is now North America, though it lived during the early Kimmeridgian, approximately 156 million years ago.

It is debated whether thermoregulation was possible for Hesperosaurus plates, as the horn sheath might have insulated them, though researchers note that cattle and ducks use horns to dissipate heat despite coverings.
